evidence: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp(service: OrderService) sends every route through OrderService methods (placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, advance, cancel, stockLevels, stockLevel) and never touches the repositories directly.
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: STATUS_BY_CODE: Record<DomainError["code"], number> is the only place that maps domain error codes to HTTP statuses.
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: parseLines only checks the body's shape (items array, productId string, quantity number) and throws DomainError('invalid_input'). No business rules are repeated here.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository. Both are plain storage adapters with no business logic.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root builds the repositories, creates OrderService(products, new InMemoryOrderRepository()) and calls createApp(service).listen(port).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/infrastructure module is one cohesive unit: it holds the adapters and the composition root for the application's ports. http-app.ts is the inbound HTTP adapter. It turns requests into OrderService calls and maps DomainError codes to HTTP statuses. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the outbound persistence adapters, which implement the ProductRepository and OrderRepository ports. server.ts wires these pieces together and starts the server. Each file uses the module's own abstractions as intended. The HTTP layer only goes through OrderService and never touches the repositories directly. The repositories implement the application ports. server.ts builds the objects through the exported constructors and createApp. No business rule is repeated. parseLines in http-app.ts only checks the shape and types of the request body at the boundary. It leaves business checks such as stock availability and state transitions to the domain and application layers. The error-to-status mapping lives in one place, STATUS_BY_CODE. One small point: the SyntaxError branch writes the literal "invalid_input" instead of using the DomainError code mapping. This is too minor to count as a duplicated invariant.
